notes: React/MUI storefront, server-side rendered (requests+BS4, no JS). Price is NOT in the visible text: read the numeric 'data-ls-price' attribute off the .lipscore-rating-small span. The listing carries no stock signal: every card says data-ls-availability="OutOfStock", and the 'Saatavuus myyjältä: Kärkkäinen' facet means 'sold by Kärkkäinen', not 'in stock' (it lists sold-out items). So availability.detail makes the runner fetch each product page and read [data-testid=product-availability-status]: 'Vain N kpl jäljellä' / 'Saatavilla N kpl' / 'Saatavilla yli 20 kpl' = in stock; 'Saatavilla jälleen <date>' = out of stock; 'Tilaustuote...' (order-in from supplier) = out of stock; 'Ennakkomyynti' = preorder. Longest text_map key wins, which keeps 'Saatavilla jälleen' ahead of 'Saatavilla'. Tilaustuote and Ennakkomyynti were not on any page when this was written (2026-10-06, 48 pages checked); their wording comes from the site's localization templates. Server-side rendering honours only ONE facet in the query string, so source_url uses the single Tuotemerkki:Pokemon facet (12 products in tests/fixtures/karkkainen.com/facets.html); a second facet is silently dropped. Cost: one extra request per Pokemon product per run. Pagination is off: the page size is 60 and the Pokemon facet is far below that.
